Plant the Moon Challenge Jr: Fall 2025 
Team: Wenceslaus Knights Gold Admin: Renee Hanson 
 Crop: Romain Lettuce Team ID: 23592 
 
Independent Variables (what we change) 
●​ Composition: 
○​ 100% Earth soil (control) + 2 worms 
○​ 100% Moon regolith simulant (control) + 2 worms 
○​ 50% Regolith / 40% Earth soil / 10% Banana peel + 2 worms 
○​ 50% Regolith / 40% Earth Soil / 5% Banana Peel / 5% egg shell + 2 worms 
○​ 50% Regolith / 50% Earth soil + 2 worms 
Amendments- Banana peel, Egg Shells, Earth Worms, Aquaponics water 
Dependent Variables (what we measure) 
●​ Germination Day 7= 75%; Day 10= 75%8 
●​ 4 Days to first emergence 
●​ At day 7 and day 10 75% of seeds had successful germination 
●​ Plant height (cm) weekly 
●​ Plant vigor/greenness rating (1–5 scale) weekly 
●​ Final fresh mass (g) at harvest 
●​ pH weekly (goal 6.0–7.0) 
Controls / Constants 
●​ Lighting: Full spectrum, 12 h ON / 12 h OFF 
●​ Temperature: 70°F in the grow tent. We used a grow tent for the entire process so we 
would have a better chance at controlling the environment. If it was too hot we could 
open a vent to cool off the temperature. It also helped us control the humidity. 
●​ Humidity: ≥50% with humidity. We filled a tin pan with water to increase humidity as 
needed, 
●​ Irrigation: Aquaponics water (same source for all pots) 60 ml per pot 2 times a week 
●​ Pot size: Identical, with drainage 
●​ Seeding: 3 romaine lettuce seeds per pot, same depth (¼ in) 
●​ Placement: Rotate positions weekly

Hypotheses- 
H1: Banana peel (B-Mix) will improve lettuce growth compared to RB-Mix because it provides 
potassium and phosphorus. 
B-Mix1 1.5g + 6.2g B-Mix2 = 7.7g fresh mass RB-Mix1 5.9g + RB-Mix2 2.4g = 10.1g fresh mass 
RB-Mix is Earth soil mixed with regolith. Regolith has minerals but plants can’t use them 
because the minerals are trapped in the regolith. We thought adding banana peel would release 
phosphorus and potassium from the regolith and help the plant grow better because it has more 
nutrients. The banana peel did not help the lettuce grow better than the Earth soil regolith mix. 
We were not correct on Hypothesis 1. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
H2: Earth soil control (CE) will outperform regolith control (CR). 
(CE1)4.9g + (CE2 (harvested wk6)) 8.9g + (CE (wk8)) 2.3g = 16.1g fresh mass 
 CR1 0.0g + CR2 0.2g = 0.2g fresh mass 
Control Earth total fresh mass was 16.1g and Control Regolith total fresh mass was 0.2g. The 
CE outperformed CR by 15.9g. We were correct on Hypothesis 2.

H3: Blends (RB-Mix, BE-Mix & B-Mix) will grow better than pure regolith and may be close to 
earth soil performance. 
CR total fresh mass = 0.2g CE total fresh mass = 16.9 g 
RB-Mix total fresh mass = 10.1g BE-Mix total fresh mass = 19.6 
B-Mix total fresh mass = 7.7g 
The Blends average fresh mass is 12.4g which is higher than the total fresh mass of CR 
which is 0.2g. The Blends outperformed the CR and one blend outperformed CE. BE-Mix 
total fresh mass is 19.6 which is higher than CE total fresh mass of 16.9. BE-Mix is 
2.7grams heavier than CE. We were correct on Hypothesis 3.

Prepare each mix. 
1.​ For B-Mix, chop banana peel in tiny pieces (~10% volume) and mix into top 2–3 cm of 
soil. Sow 3 romaine seeds per pot at ¼ inches. 
2.​ Water with aquaponics water source 60 mm each pot. 
3.​ Place all pots in a grow tent at 70°F, 12/12 light, Humidity at 50% or higher. 
Days 1–10 – Germination 
●​ Sowing date September 29, 2025 
●​ Germination day 7 - 75%. Day 10 75% 
●​ heating mat during the germination process on day 2 
●​ Added 2 Earth worms to each pot on 10-10-25 
Weeks 2–5 – Growth 
●​ Thin to 1 healthiest seedling per pot after 2–3 true leaves. 
●​ Added sticks to keep leaves up 
●​ Added hay to keep leaves off soil regolith mix 
●​ We added vinegar in small containers with holes in the top to capture gnats that 
appeared weak 3 
●​ Fan on day 1 of week 4 to simulate wind movement because the leaves were looking 
like they were droopy and starting to get brown spots 
Week 6 – Recorded height, leaf count, vigor, fresh mass (g), pH and observations.

Week 7 - Recorded height, leaf count, vigor, fresh mass (g), pH and observations. We picked 
CE2 because we thought 100% Earth soil had the best nutrients and best chance to grow after 
the harvest. CE2 produced 8.9g of fresh mass.

pages.text:
What we would do differently: 
1.​ We forgot to list the BE-Mix with a label in our initial design report so we added it to all 
data collection sheets and to the final report. 
2.​ We should have washed the egg shells with warm water before adding them to the mix. 
The raw egg white may have contaminated the plant and caused the brown spots in 
weeks 4-8. 
3.​ The ID “RB” is confusing because it makes us think it is only Regolith & Banana mix and 
it is Regolith and Earth. We should have labeled it RE for Regolith & Earth mix. 
4.​ Lower our temperature to 65 degrees Fahrenheit to produce crisp lettuce that is not bitter 
 
Successes: 
75% of our pots germinated by day 10. 
 
Week 4 our plants are growing at the perfect rate. They look healthy and have a perfect PH. 
They are green and have many leaves. 
 
Watering 2 times a week with 60 ml of aquaponics water is keeping them in good health. 
 
We have been able to keep the temperature at 70 degrees without much effort. 
 
We got faster at checking pH so we were no longer late for the next class. 
 
We learned to work together and listen to each other. 
 
We learned how to use a digital caliper to measure stem height and we learned that mm are 
very small. 
 
We learned how to measure mass and what mass is. 
 
Challenges: 
Two of our plants grew mushrooms/fungi by week 3. We removed the mushrooms and they 
have not grown back. 
The plants that germinated in the regolith control pots have since died. 
 
We added a fan to imitate the wind so the lettuce will grow to its fullest. Our school lost power in 
week 4. We did not notice the fan turned off for 4 days. We did notice more brown spots on 
several plants. We did some research and found that either they have a fungus or they need 
movement from the wind. We checked the fan and noticed it was off. 
 
It is hard to write down the correct data in the correct spot every time so we added a second 
person watching and making sure we do it right.

The humidity gets too high and too low. We have to open vents or add a shallow pan of water to 
fix the humidity and we do not have access to the grow tent 24 hours a day 7 days a week. 
 
Sometimes we want to go to recess instead of checking pH or measuring growth. 
It is difficult to get to school early to monitor the plants and collect data when you do not drive or 
live. So the students who live close enough to walk to school were assigned the before school 
jobs just in case the students who needed rides could not make it. 
 
We broke several leaves while collecting data. We decided we were going too fast and had to 
slow down so we did not break any more leaves.
